title: Acme Git sync: publish your site on every merge
description: Keep landing pages and docs in your repository, review them in pull requests with previews, and publish on merge. See how it works.

settings.title: Your website, *reviewed like code*
settings.description: Pages and docs live in your repository. Every pull request gets a preview; every merge publishes.

media.alt: A pull request with an Acme preview check

items.title: Connect a repository
items.description: Pick the repository, branch and site folder in Settings.

items.title: Open a pull request
items.description: Edit JSON pages or Markdown docs; a preview check links to the result.

items.title: Merge
items.description: Acme validates every file and publishes them together, or not at all.

settings.title: Previews before anything goes live
settings.body:
Every pull request that touches your pages gets a **private preview**, so reviewers see the real page, not a diff.

- Desktop and mobile

- Light and dark mode

- Unindexed and expiring

settings.title: Roll back in one click
settings.body: Each merge is a release. If something looks wrong, activate the previous release from the dashboard and fix forward in Git.

settings.title: Included in every plan
settings.description: Git sync costs nothing extra. See all plans on the [pricing page](/pricing).

items.question: Can I still edit pages in the dashboard?
items.answer: Yes. Dashboard edits become pull requests, so the repository stays the source of truth.

items.question: What happens if a file is invalid?
items.answer: Nothing changes on your live site. The problem, with file and line, shows in the dashboard and on the pull request.

items.question: Do I have to move my existing pages by hand?
items.answer: No. Export them to the repository in one pull request, then merge it.
